activities.body: Review the model and note the main prewar pattern.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions shaped a divided Europe before 1914.

activities.label: Own words
activities.title: Why the crisis widened
activities.body: Answer from memory in 2 or 3 sentences. Then compare your wording to the model.
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination set off the July Crisis, then mobilization and declarations of war widened the conflict.
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination in Sarajevo triggered the July Crisis, and then mobilization and declarations of war spread the conflict into a wider war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the assassination, the July Crisis, and how mobilization and declarations of war widened the conflict.

activities.label: Fix the gap
activities.title: Repair the outbreak sequence
activities.body: Correct the missing link in the sequence. Then give one revised sentence.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking the assassination alone immediately became a general war, without the July Crisis and declarations of war in between.
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination set off the July Crisis, then mobilization and declarations of war widened the conflict.
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination started the July Crisis, and then mobilization and declarations of war widened the conflict.
activities.feedback: The key correction is that the assassination was the trigger, but the war widened through the July Crisis and state decisions to mobilize and declare war.

activities.label: Timeline check
activities.title: WWI timeline in order
activities.body: Explain the WWI start-to-finish timeline from memory in one short chain.
activities.concept: From 1914 to 1918, the war moved from outbreak to U.S. entry and then to the armistice.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the war ended with the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: A complete answer keeps the order clear: outbreak in 1914, U.S. entry in 1917, armistice in 1918.

activities.title: Match the cause map
activities.body: Choose the best summary of the WWI outbreak and timeline.

World War I began in 1914, the United States entered in 1915, and the armistice ended the war in 1917.
The war started with the armistice in 1918, then the United States entered, and the Sarajevo assassination came later.
World War I was only a short border dispute that ended before 1915.

activities.title: Europe before 1914
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided Europe into rival blocs before 1914.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: Europe before 1914
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances shape tensions before 1914?
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided Europe into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival alliance blocs, which increased mistrust and made a wider war more likely.
activities.feedback: The alliances mattered because they hardened rivalry, not because they prevented conflict.

activities.body: What happened after the Sarajevo assassination to turn the crisis into war?
